title: How do you generate sounds/music for your games?
author: uchilles2020
selftext: Wondering if anyone has suggestions on how to generate good sound effects and music for AI games? Opus 5 does great work with graphics but can't seem to get great results on sounds.

comments.author: Juannieve05
comments.body: There are royalty free libraries with good music, good enough for a concept, if you are ready to release? It is better to get actual licenses of actual music

replies.author: uchilles2020
replies.body: Any sources that you recommend for these?

replies.author: vurt72
replies.body: why would you use a generic library that others would have used as well, in the age of AI music??

comments.author: dragolineage01
comments.body: You can now try MiniMax Music 3.0, its pretty great given its local

comments.author: TheCelestialBubble
comments.body: Eleven labs has a free tier but I think you can't use it for commercial purposes. Like 8£ for a starter license tho which u can use in commercial areas. Decent amount of credits. You'll go through hard if u start generating several minute songs after a while but sound effects are cheap as chips. Do have to normally go through a few takes tho

replies.body: Half joke half serious, but how would they even know

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body: For music, I use Suno free tier.  I just describe it and then download the mp3, open it in Reaper (or any DAW) and make it into a repeating loop.  For sound effects I use whatever I can find and record off my pc.  If I was going to sell the games, Id make sure they were ok to use but I’m not so I just record anything.

replies.author: ChillRefill
replies.body: Suno free tier does not allow you to use it ever commercially, you need to have generated it under a paid plan. Just FYI.

comments.author: asd849849494984984
comments.body: pixabay for sound effects. For music idk, ai doesn't seem to good at it, unless it's modern stuff.

comments.author: Evoroth
comments.body:
I already did chip tunes for a game and then created a Python script to turn those into better quality tracks. 

I’ve then turned that into a skill for AI for things in the future and it’s worked great for placeholder tracks - ultimately all building tracks and effects with Python and the output being ogg. 

There’s lots of less involved options too though like others have mentioned: pixabay, suno, etc. there’s also the free GDV libraries from Soniss

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: For VO, I'm using the first paid tier (US$7?) for elevenlabs. I think I'll get something like 80 lines of finished dialogue for the 40k tokens I get a month, because I will get some wonkly mispronunciations and I'll spend a few thousand credites creating custom character voices. For music/SFX - I've purchased several audio packs with indie-game friendly distribution licenses over the years with both SFX and music, so I'm picking the best of what I got for what I need for my game these and spelunking through old email receipts to confirm the usage rights before I ship the game.

replies.author: WantedRogue
replies.body: Good point about the text to speech in Elevenlabs, it’s actually very good.

comments.author: WantedRogue
comments.body:
I use Elevenlabs for sound effects and Suno for music. Just make sure you have the necessary license. Any effects or music you generate before you have the correct license can’t be used even if you subsequently buy the license. 

I find Elevenlabs to be a bit fiddly, I end up use Gemini to help me get the right prompt. Without a paid tier I burn through tokens. There may be a better sound effects AI.

comments.author: CubeUnleashed
comments.body: I would recommend spending money on sfx or music packs, there are many ressources on itch or if it has to be free, I often check out freesounds org and filter for CC0 license. Suno is more miss than hit in my opinion, but there's always the option to download stems there and mix them to your liking.

comments.author: Iteration-k
comments.body: Try Elevenlabs.io You can generate a bunch of music and sound effects and even music

comments.author: fitm3
comments.body: I know tts local models exist but I haven’t got one working on my machine actually.  I hooked Claude up to comfy ui local mcp and it does a good job on music with stable audio.  It’s done a good job with sound effects too that it procedurally generates. Except for like groans for zombies.

comments.author: CleverAdvisorPrime
comments.body: I've been using https://www.minimax.io/audio/music. and it's been really good.

comments.author: Level-Physics-1730
comments.body: Splice has awesome game sound layers/oneshots and you can get about 200 sounds from ANY high end sound pack you want for like 5$ (they have "cheap first 20$ later" style subscriptions all the time). You can have opus 5/fable 5 mix them together using python DSP if you want unique sounds out of the layers, there's also the 20gb+ worth of free sound layers by filmcow [https://filmcow.itch.io/filmcow-sfx](https://filmcow.itch.io/filmcow-sfx) I wouldn't recommend AI generating any sound for anything it 100% of the time sounds like shit, have the model mix layers instead.
